object.question: How do Alliance Revolt and Spread Sympathy differ in timing/order, eligible clearing, supporter cost, martial law and results?

answerKey.canonicalization: UTF-8 JSON, sorted keys, compact separators, ensure_ascii=false

object.expected_answer: Birdsong Revolt before Spread, each any number. Revolt: sympathetic clearing without base whose matching base is on board, pay two matching supporters, remove all enemy pieces, place matching base, warriors equal matching sympathetic clearings, one officer, score removed enemy buildings/tokens. Spread: unsympathetic adjacent to sympathy or any clearing if none; pay shown matching supporters plus one if at least three warriors of one other player; place sympathy and score uncovered points.

source_passages.section: Woodland Alliance — Birdsong Revolt and Spread Sympathy
source_passages.quotation:
**Birdsong:** Both Revolt and Spread Sympathy take place **during Birdsong**. Complete **all Revolts before starting any Spread Sympathy**; each may be performed any number of times. **For both actions, every supporter spent must match the target clearing; birds are wild.** Once spreading starts, you cannot return to Revolt this Birdsong, so newly spread sympathy cannot support a same-Birdsong Revolt:

- **Revolt:** Choose sympathetic clearing without a base, matching a base still on your board. Spend **two matching supporters**. **Remove all enemy pieces there and score one VP per enemy building/token removed**; then place matching base. Place warriors there equal to number of sympathetic clearings matching the base's printed suit (including revolt clearing), and one warrior in Officers box. Score normal VP for removed enemy buildings/tokens. Resolve the effect even if a prompted placement cannot be completed: place the maximum possible, without adding a base-placement prerequisite. Enemy Vagabond damages three items instead of being removed.
- **Spread Sympathy:** Choose unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy; if no sympathy anywhere, choose any clearing. Spend matching supporters shown above next sympathy token. **Martial Law:** add one matching supporter if chosen clearing has at least three warriors of **one other player**. Place token and score uncovered space. Only one sympathy per clearing. Keep's placement ban still applies.

answer.part: Timing, order and shared supporter suit
answer.ruling: Revolt and Spread Sympathy both occur during Birdsong. Complete all Revolts before starting Spread Sympathy; either action may be performed any number of times. Every supporter spent for either action must match the target clearing, with birds wild. Once spreading starts, Revolt cannot resume that Birdsong, so new sympathy cannot fund a same-Birdsong Revolt.
answer.evidence: Woodland Alliance — Birdsong Revolt and Spread Sympathy

answer.ruling: Choose a sympathetic clearing without a base that matches a base still on your board. Spend two matching supporters. Remove all enemy pieces there, scoring one VP per enemy building or token removed, then place the matching base. Place warriors there equal to the number of sympathetic clearings matching that base’s printed suit, including the revolt clearing, and one warrior in the Officers box. Score normal VP for enemy buildings/tokens removed. If a prompted placement is short, place the maximum possible; this does not add a base-placement prerequisite. An enemy Vagabond damages three items instead of being removed.

answer.part: Spread Sympathy eligibility, cost, Martial Law and result
answer.ruling: Choose an unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy, or any clearing if there is no sympathy anywhere. Spend the number of supporters shown above the next sympathy token, matching that target clearing. If the chosen clearing has at least three warriors of one other player, Martial Law adds one matching supporter. Place the sympathy token and score the uncovered VP space. Only one sympathy token is allowed per clearing, and the Keep’s placement ban remains.

sourceEvidence.quotation: Your Birdsong has two steps in the following order. ... Revolt. Any number of times ... Choose a sympathetic clearing without a base that matches a base on your faction board. ... Spend two supporters matching the suit of the chosen clearing. ... Remove all enemy pieces from the chosen clearing. Then, place the matching base there, and place warriors there equal to the number of sympathetic clearings matching the base’s printed suit. Finally, place one warrior in the Officers box. ... (Remember to score one victory point per token and building removed.)
sourceEvidence.application: Revolt is the first Birdsong step; its eligibility, two-card cost, removal, base, clearing warriors, officer, and one-point ordinary removal award are explicit.

sourceEvidence.quotation: Spread Sympathy. Any number of times ... Choose an unsympathetic clearing adjacent to a sympathetic clearing. If there are no sympathetic clearings, you may choose any clearing. ... Spend supporters matching the suit of the chosen clearing. The number of supporters that must be spent is listed above the sympathy token. ... Martial Law. You must spend another matching supporter if the target clearing has at least 3 warriors of another player, including warriors they are treating as their own for rule (Mercenaries, hirelings, etc.). ... Place a sympathy token in the chosen clearing. Score the victory points on the space uncovered on your faction board.
sourceEvidence.application: Second Birdsong step; each use has its own eligibility and cost. Martial Law modifies Spread Sympathy, not Revolt.

sourceEvidence.quotation: Whenever you remove an enemy’s building or token, you score one victory point.
sourceEvidence.application: The one point per removed enemy building/token in Revolt is the normal removal award, not a separate faction bonus.

sourceEvidence.quotation: Your Birdsong has two steps in the following order. ... Can I revolt with a base in a suit whose base I've already built? ... Nope! The revolt action says you must choose a sympathetic clearing matching an unbuilt base. ... Step 3: Resolve Effect. Remove all enemy pieces ... (Remember to score one victory point per token and building removed.)
sourceEvidence.application: The complete official same-question section independently agrees with the extracted Law, including the reminder nature of removal scoring. Its Keep FAQ explains that ordinary play cannot establish sympathy at the Keep.

sourceEvidence.quotation: You can treat any bird card as a card of another suit, even if you must spend, take, or give multiple cards of the same suit.
sourceEvidence.application: Bird supporters can satisfy either action’s matching-suit payments, including the extra Martial Law supporter.

sourceEvidence.quotation: If you are prompted to place, take, or remove pieces but you cannot do so fully, you must place, take, or remove the maximum number possible. (This does not let you avoid costs or prerequisites. You just cannot do less than the most you can.)
sourceEvidence.application: After legal Revolt selection and payment, short placement does not cancel the effect. Having the matching base on the faction board is an actual selection prerequisite; successful base placement is not listed as an additional prerequisite.

sourceEvidence.quotation: The Vagabond pawn cannot be removed from the map. ... Whenever an enemy player uses an effect that says it removes all enemy pieces from a clearing (such as Alliance revolts ... ) with the Vagabond, the Vagabond damages three items.
sourceEvidence.application: The volunteered Vagabond exception correctly limits the general all-enemy-pieces instruction.

sourceEvidence.quotation: A clearing can hold only one sympathy token. ... A sympathetic clearing is one with a sympathy token. An unsympathetic clearing is one without a sympathy token.
sourceEvidence.application: Supports the single-token limit and why the revolt clearing itself counts among matching sympathetic clearings.

sourceEvidence.quotation: The Marquise can place pieces in the clearing with the keep token, and other players cannot.
sourceEvidence.application: Spread Sympathy must obey the Keep placement ban; neither answer asserts a bypass.

sourceEvidence.quotation: A clearing is adjacent to all other clearings linked to it by a path.
sourceEvidence.application: The volunteered by-path clarification correctly defines Spread Sympathy adjacency.

Two supporters matching the target clearing.

Target-matching supporters equal to the printed cost above the next sympathy token.
Only Spread Sympathy pays one additional matching supporter when the target has at least three warriors of one other player.
Place sympathy in the selected clearing and score the newly uncovered VP space.

exactScoringAnalysis.sourceRule: Law 3.2.1 awards one point whenever an enemy building/token is removed. Law 8.4.1.III expressly reminds the Alliance to score that same one point. Revolt contains no separate point award added to ordinary removal VP.
exactScoringAnalysis.method: Read each complete Q15 quotation and answer together, identifying the subject, removed pieces, amount, and modifier of each scoring statement. Repetition alone does not establish an additional scoring event; an actual instruction adding another award would be materially wrong even if the requested comparison were otherwise complete.

readerA.firstExactSentence: Remove all enemy pieces there, scoring one VP per enemy building or token removed, then place the matching base.
readerA.laterExactSentence: Score normal VP for enemy buildings/tokens removed.
readerA.quotationAlsoRepeats: The cited full summary passage gives one VP per removed enemy building/token and later says Score normal VP for removed enemy buildings/tokens.
readerA.interpretation: The later sentence labels the same removal award normal VP and repeats the same enemy building/token referent. It supplies no different trigger, amount, extra modifier, or second award. In the complete list of Revolt results it restates the normal removal points already described in the removal sentence. This is redundant phrasing; reading it as another one VP each would require treating the repeated reminder as a separate payment instruction without wording that distinguishes one.

readerB.firstExactSentence: Remove all enemy pieces there, scoring one VP for each enemy building or token removed, then place the matching base.
readerB.laterExactSentence: Score normal VP for buildings/tokens removed as well.
readerB.quotationAlsoRepeats: The full quoted source passage first specifies one VP per enemy building/token removed and later repeats normal removal VP, without a separate bonus.
readerB.interpretation: The words as well add normal removal scoring to the surrounding list of Revolt results (base, clearing warriors, officer), while redundantly mentioning the same award already attached to removal. Normal VP identifies the ordinary one-point-per-building/token award; it does not identify another faction award. The complete response never states two points, another point, score again, or a normal award in addition to a distinct Revolt bonus. Although as well makes the duplication less tidy, the repeated subject and normal label support one award rather than a second award. This conclusion follows the whole wording, rather than deleting as well or treating every repeated scoring sentence as additive.

exactScoringAnalysis.application: If Revolt removes two enemy buildings and one enemy token, the removal award described by each complete response is three VP. Neither response prescribes six. Warriors do not receive a removal VP in either response.
exactScoringAnalysis.ambiguityLimit: The duplicated sentences could be edited for clarity, especially Reader B’s as well, but awkward repetition is not itself a material false rule. If a response had expressly added another removal award on top of the first, it would be incorrect under the supplied grading standard.
